comparator.name: Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics
comparator.academicYear: Current UvA PPLE curriculum structure, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme structure totals 180 EC: a 102-EC compulsory shared interdisciplinary core, 66 EC in the selected specialisation together with the Bachelor’s thesis, and 12 EC of electives. The generic target offers Politics, Psychology, Law and Economics specialisations. None is identified as the broad default; Politics is first in the official programme name and curriculum order and is selected by the neutral official-order tie-break before UCR course selection. The official source publishes the shared core and major/thesis as formal aggregate credit buckets, which are preserved rather than subdivided without evidence.
components: Compulsory interdisciplinary core curriculum: eight interdisciplinary courses, four integrative seminars and four methodological courses
The current official programme structure reports this compulsory shared core as 102 EC.
The current official structure reports specialisation courses and the thesis together as 66 EC; Politics is selected using the neutral official-order tie-break.
Genuine elective space is preserved without inventing particular courses.

routeSelection.basis: The generic bachelor requires one of four equally presented disciplinary specialisations and identifies no broad default. Politics appears first in the official programme name and curriculum order, so it is selected neutrally before and independently of UCR course selection.

core: Integrated analysis of social problems through politics, psychology, law and economics
Political power, governance, institutions, democracy and public policy
Human behaviour, social psychology, decision-making and behavioural approaches to public problems
Law, legal reasoning, justice, morality and the institutional foundations of society
Microeconomics, macroeconomics, behavioural economics and the economic dimensions of social challenges
Interdisciplinary research design, qualitative and quantitative methods, statistics and independent inquiry
adjacent: Behavioural public policy and the psychology of political and economic decisions
questions: How can political, psychological, legal and economic evidence be integrated to understand contemporary social problems?
How do human behaviour and decision-making shape public institutions and policy?
How do law, justice and economic institutions organise power, incentives and social outcomes?

alternatives.label: Politics, psychology, law & economics
alternatives.concept: Integrates political institutions and international relations with social psychology, legal reasoning, economics and empirical methods to examine contemporary social problems from all four fields represented in PPLE.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has sustained political, psychological, legal and economic strands rather than allowing any one field to stand for the whole programme.
progression: Political, economic, legal, psychological and research foundations precede advanced public economics, constitutional and international law, behavioural economics, psychology and governance. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Behavioural public policy & economic decision-making
alternatives.concept: Organises the four fields around behavioural public policy: psychology and behavioural economics explain decision-making, while politics, law, data and public economics examine how institutions design and evaluate interventions.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum’s centre of gravity is behavioural and economic explanation of public decisions, supported by political institutions, law and quantitative analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad four-field plan, this route gives substantially more weight to psychology, behavioural economics, data and policy evaluation and less to international history and global governance. More than four courses differ, and the organising question shifts to how behaviour and incentives shape public intervention.
progression: Brain and behaviour, political institutions, economics and methods precede experimental psychology, public economics, behavioural economics, econometrics and advanced law and policy. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Law, justice & economic governance
alternatives.concept: Organises the four fields around justice and governance, combining public, international, constitutional and private law with politics, economics, social psychology and negotiation to examine how institutions allocate rights, power and resources.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed plan is anchored in law and justice but retains material political, economic and behavioural study of institutions and decisions.
alternatives.distinctness: This route replaces much of the international-governance and data emphasis of the closest plan and the behavioural-policy emphasis of the second plan with a sustained public, private, constitutional, European and international law sequence. It differs from each earlier curriculum by more than 30 EC.
progression: Law, political philosophy, psychology, economics and methods foundations precede public, private, constitutional, European and international law, advanced politics and behavioural economics. All formal prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

selection.assessment: The first plan is the closest integrated response to PPLE across its four named disciplines. The behavioural-public-policy and law/justice/economic-governance directions are separately supported by direct and stable programme interests, produce coherent curricula and pass the pairwise 30-EC distinctness floor. Production therefore stops at the maximum of three.

blocks: The official 66-EC bucket combines the selected Politics specialisation with the thesis; it cannot be aligned one-to-one with a single 7.5-EC UCR course.
Interdisciplinary methods, development and choice space
The official 102-EC shared core integrates sixteen compulsory courses across four fields and methods; no single UCR course reproduces this aggregate component.
The comparator preserves 12 EC of genuine elective space, which has no fixed subject counterpart in the selected UCR curricula.

notes.text: PPLE has a compulsory 102-EC interdisciplinary core followed by one formal disciplinary specialisation and a Bachelor’s thesis. UCR can combine substantial politics, psychology, law, economics and methods study, but it does not reproduce PPLE’s integrated course sequence, small-cohort seminars or formal major structure.
